newsitem.title: GERMANY: No initial comment on report Holzmann CEO may go.
newsitem.headline: No initial comment on report Holzmann CEO may go.

text.p: Spokesmen for Philipp Holzmann AG and Metallgesellschaft AG were not immediately able to comment on Friday on a newspaper report that Holzmann's chief executive may be sacked and replaced by the head of MG.

The report in mass circulation daily "Bild," which quoted the Munich-based news service "dossier B," said Holzmann chief executive Lothar Mayer faced dismissal because of losses on a real estate project.
An auditor's report by accountants KPMG on the losses would be presented to Holzmann's supervisory board on Tuesday, October 8, Bild said.
A spokesman for Holzmann contacted by Reuters said the supervisory board was due to meet on Thursday, not Tuesday, but he was unable to provide further information immediately.
"I can't say anything on that yet," the Holzmann spokesman said.
The Bild report also said Kajo Neukirchen, the management board chairman of MG, was being mooted as a possible successor to Mayer. An MG spokesman was unable to comment immediately.
Holzmann said in August that it aimed to break even in 1996 as special earnings would offset an expected operating loss.

The group said it would dissolve some hidden reserves in order to compensate for the operating loss as well as for possible losses on property sales and write-offs associated with a restructuring of its portfolio.

Holzmann ran into financial problems in 1995, posting an unexpected loss of 443 million marks which forced it to omit its dividend payout. At the root of its problems were 458 million marks of write-downs on its property portfolio.
Holzmann on Wednesday denied a radio report that the group had liquidity problems.
